title: Equivariant finite-family prism homotopy on continuous cochains
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field]. For a topological group $J$ and a topological $E$-vector space $V$ with jointly continuous $E$-linear $J$-action, write $B^n(J,V)$ for the abstract $E$-vector space of jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ with $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$. Its differential is $(\delta F)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^jF(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_{n+1})$, and it is extended by zero in negative degrees. Let $G$ be a topological group, $S$ a finite set (possibly empty), and $a_s:G\to G$ continuous maps for $s\in S$. Assume that for every $a\in G$ there is a permutation $\pi_a:S\to S$ such that $a_s(ax)=a a_{\pi_a(s)}(x)$ for every $s\in S$ and $x\in G$. For every topological $E$-vector space $V$ with jointly continuous linear $G$-action, define
$$(L_{V,n}F)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{s\in S}F(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_n)).$$
Then $L_V$ is an $E$-linear endomorphism of $B^\bullet(G,V)$ as a cochain complex. Set $K_{V,0}=0:B^0(G,V)\to0$ and, for $n\geq1$, define
$$(K_{V,n}F)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})=\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_{n-1})).$$
These are well-defined $E$-linear maps $B^n(G,V)\to B^{n-1}(G,V)$, with continuous and $G$-equivariant values, and satisfy
$$\delta K_{V,n}+K_{V,n+1}\delta=L_{V,n}-|S|\,\mathrm{id}_{B^n(G,V)}\qquad(n\geq0).$$
In degree zero the identity is $K_{V,1}\delta F(x_0)=\sum_s(F(a_s(x_0))-F(x_0))$. With the same finite family $(a_s)$ the construction is simultaneously natural in coefficients: for every continuous equivariant $E$-linear $b:V\to W$, postcomposition satisfies $b_*L_{V,n}=L_{W,n}b_*$ and $b_*K_{V,n}=K_{W,n}b_*$ in every degree. No compactness of $G$, or completeness, local compactness, Hausdorffness or discreteness of $V$ is required.

proof.text: The spaces $B^n$ are vector subspaces of all functions under pointwise operations: finite sums and scalar multiples preserve continuity and equivariance. The deletion differential preserves these subspaces for the same reason and is linear. For $0\leq p<q\leq n+2$, deleting positions $p$ then $q-1$, or $q$ then $p$, gives the same tuple with opposite signs $(-1)^{p+q-1}$ and $(-1)^{q+p}$. Thus $\delta^2=0$, including the zero negative degrees. For $L$, deleting a coordinate commutes with applying $a_s$ to all coordinates; interchanging its two finite sums gives $\delta L_n=L_{n+1}\delta$.

proof.text:
Each tuple map appearing in $L_n$ or $K_n$ has coordinates that are projections or a continuous $a_s$ composed with a projection. Composing with $F$ and taking finite signed sums proves continuity of their values, and pointwise linearity proves $E$-linearity. Fix $a\in G$ and choose the single permutation $\pi_a$ from the hypothesis, which works for all coordinates. Equivariance of $F$ gives
$$F(a_s(ax_0),\ldots,a_s(ax_n))=aF(a_{\pi_a(s)}(x_0),\ldots,a_{\pi_a(s)}(x_n)),$$
and, in a prism summand,
$$F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_i,a_s(ax_i),\ldots,a_s(ax_{n-1}))=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_{\pi_a(s)}(x_i),\ldots,a_{\pi_a(s)}(x_{n-1})).$$
Reindexing $s$ by the bijection $\pi_a$ and using linearity of the action proves equivariance of both sums. Hence the operators have exactly the stated domains and codomains, with $K_0=0$. No continuity or compatibility in $a$ of the chosen permutations is needed.

proof.text:
For the algebraic identity use [lem-trf-coefficient-bar-prism-homotopy]. For a fixed $s$, take both indexing categories to have object set the underlying set of $G$ and exactly one arrow between any ordered pair of objects. This is small in a universe containing $G$. The object maps $v=\mathrm{id}$ and $w=a_s$ extend uniquely to functors, and the unique arrows $x\to a_s(x)$ give a natural transformation: every naturality square has the same unique composite. Take $R=E$, both coefficient functors constant with value $E$ and all restriction maps identities, and $t=\mathrm{id}$. A chain $U_q\to\cdots\to U_0$ corresponds to the ordered tuple $(x_0,\ldots,x_q)=(U_q,\ldots,U_0)$. Concretely this direct sum consists of finitely supported coefficient families $(c_t)$ indexed by tuples $t$. The coordinate vectors $[t]$ give the unique expansion $(c_t)=\sum_t c_t[t]$, so they form a basis in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Its boundary $\partial$ is alternating deletion, since all coefficient restrictions are identities. The cited prism maps become
$$H^s_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]=\sum_{i=0}^q(-1)^i[x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_q)].$$
Its asserted chain identity is therefore $\partial H^s_q+H^s_{q-1}\partial=(a_s)_*-\mathrm{id}$, where $H^s_{-1}=0$ and the unaugmented boundary out of degree zero is zero. Identity arrows and repeated vertices are allowed by the cited statement.

proof.text:
For a function $F:G^{n+1}\to V$, define evaluation on the free module by $\widetilde F(\sum_t c_t[t])=\sum_t c_tF(t)$. Unique finite basis expansion in [def-weil-pbc-free-module] makes this well-defined and linear. Direct evaluation gives $\widetilde{\delta F}=\widetilde F\partial$ and, for $n\geq1$, the single-$s$ prism operator $K^s_nF=\widetilde F H^s_{n-1}$ on tuples. Evaluating the preceding chain identity in degree $n$ consequently gives
$$\delta K^s_nF+K^s_{n+1}\delta F=F\circ a_s^{\times(n+1)}-F.$$
For $n=0$ only $H^s_0$ occurs, giving $K^s_1\delta F(x)=F(a_s(x))-F(x)$. Sum over $s$ to obtain precisely $\delta K_n+K_{n+1}\delta=L_n-|S|\,\mathrm{id}$. By step 2 this equality of functions is an equality in $B^n$; individual $K^s_n$ need not preserve equivariance. If $S$ is empty every operator and both sides are zero.

proof.text: A continuous equivariant linear map $b:V\to W$ sends $B^n(G,V)$ to $B^n(G,W)$ by composition. For each tuple, $b(\sum_s F(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_n)))=\sum_s (b\circ F)(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_n))$; moving $b$ through the finite signed double sum proves the identical assertion for $K_n$, also for $K_0=0$. Thus the fixed family gives both naturalities simultaneously for every $b$. All topology arguments used only continuity of the maps, finite products and finite vector-space operations, so no stated excluded topological assumption has entered.
